title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
why_read: A surprising and well-isolated finding that most of the benefit from expensive RL fine-tuning of image/video diffusion models can be captured by a tiny, fixed, prompt-independent steering vector.
analysis: The researchers tested whether reinforcement learning fine-tuning of diffusion transformers (used for AI image and video generation) actually learns complex prompt-specific adjustments, or something simpler. They found that a constant vector added to internal activations, identical regardless of the input prompt, can recover 90 percent or more of the quality gains from full RL fine-tuning while using 65 times fewer parameters. This suggests RL post-training mostly nudges the model toward outputs it could already produce rather than teaching new input-dependent reasoning. The result has real implications for how efficiently these models can be tuned and what RL fine-tuning is actually doing mechanistically.
